metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after sharp spikes; reduce initial forecast peaks by 5–10%.
- After a price spike, model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward quickly; apply a “cool-down” decay factor to subsequent forecasts.
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model exhibits strong mean-reversion bias — overcorrects toward historical averages; adjust for recent volatility.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in capturing true price drops; delay downward revisions by 1–2 periods unless sentiment shifts.
- If true outcome shows sharp downward trend after a peak, model fails to anticipate it; add a “reversal trigger” rule: if 3 consecutive days drop >2% from peak, reduce forecast by 3–5%.
- Sentiment history is static (all 0.00) — no behavioral signal — so model should not assume sentiment-driven volatility; treat as pure technical correction.
